subject: Private GPU Pool: demand cadence, allocation proposal & egress throttling
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Anya Petrova <anya@vectorai.com>
Cc: Tom Lin <tom.lin@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 08:14:00 -0800
Subject: Private GPU Pool: demand cadence, allocation proposal & egress throttling

Hi all —

Following up from last week's capacity working group. VectorAI's pilot looks like it will ramp faster than our original projection (see attached q4_demand_forecast_v3.xlsx). Before we lock commitments I want to propose a short cadence and the allocation/egress controls we should apply to keep both latency and egress cost predictable for the customer and our fleet.

Proposal (high level):
- Weekly allocation windows for guaranteed quota + daily burst pool for transient traffic (burst pool capped per-tenant).
- Network egress throttle templates to apply at the VPC edge when sustained > X MB/s per tenant (attached YAML).
- Warm-cache steering for high-QPS prefixes to reduce tail latency during bursts.

Asks: can infra size the guaranteed pool for VectorAI to 12 sustained TPUs-equivalent slots (approx 240 qps aggregate at their average prompt length) and expose a burst cap of +50% for 6 hours/day? Karthik — can you sanity-check the numbers in the spreadsheet and call out any network constraints? Vivek — can you confirm thermal and admission implications for evening windows? Anya — any procurement constraints on burst windows from your side?

Attaching: q4_demand_forecast_v3.xlsx, egress-throttle-config-templates.yaml, network-topology-v2.pdf

Thanks —
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Anya Petrova <anya@vectorai.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private GPU Pool: demand cadence, allocation proposal & egress throttling

Hannah — TL;DR the computed sustained slots look reasonable but a few callouts:

1) Network headroom: the topology PDF shows the customer colocation link provisioned at 10 Gbps. With the forecasted peak (sheet tab 'peak_paths') we hit ~6.2 Gbps sustained if they use embeddings-heavy workloads; that leaves ~3.8 Gbps for overhead (replication, metrics, backup). We should either increase guaranteed network reservation or limit sustained burst egress to ~4 Gbps to avoid cross-tenant impact.

2) Allocation math: the 12-slot guarantee maps to 180 concurrent contexts (we estimate ~15 tokens/sec per slot average). If VectorAI's prompt distribution skews longer tails (doc-heavy), our effective qps could drop. Recommend we add a tunable soft-limit per-tenant on sequence length in the admission policy.

3) Autoscale cadence: weekly guaranteed + daily 6-hour burst is fine operationally, but suggest implementing a 3-step ramp (10% -> 50% -> 100% over 30 mins) for burst enablement to avoid cache stampedes.

I'll annotate the spreadsheet and push comments to the Drive link.

- Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Infra Engineer
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Anya Petrova <anya@vectorai.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 12:21:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private GPU Pool: demand cadence, allocation proposal & egress throttling

Hannah — quick operational notes from an admission/thermal perspective:

- Evening window (1800-2400 local) has historically higher thermal constraints for the target colo racks; sustaining +50% burst for 6 hours may push some racks into thermal mitigation territory. If VectorAI's burst overlaps with other customers' spikes, we risk thermal throttling and reduced throughput.
- Mitigation: prefer staggered burst windows per tenant and enforce the 3-step ramp Karthik suggested. Also enable pre-warm for KV caches 20 minutes before burst start.

I'll run a quick simulation against last quarter's telemetry and share a heatmap by rack by EOD.

Vivek
Director, Fleet Reliability
From: Anya Petrova <anya@vectorai.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Lin <tom.lin@acme.com>, procurement@acme.com
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 13:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private GPU Pool: demand cadence, allocation proposal & egress throttling

Thanks everyone — this is helpful. A few notes from VectorAI:
- Procurement: the contract team is OK with a guaranteed allocation + burst structure but needs clear SLOs for burst availability (we will ask for credits if bursts are unavailable > 2 days/month).
- We can shift our heavy batch jobs to off-peak and would prefer burst windows of 0300-0900 UTC (local-night). That should help the thermal profile.
- One ask: can Redwood expose a per-burst telemetry feed (simple CSV per day) so we can reconcile egress usage against billing?

Anya
Anya Petrova
Head of Platform, VectorAI
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Anya Petrova <anya@vectorai.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 16:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private GPU Pool: demand cadence, allocation proposal & egress throttling

Thanks — good alignment. Action items:
- Karthik: update spreadsheet with network-safe burst cap (4 Gbps) and add the 3-step ramp into the admission policy doc. Link the updated sheet: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cForecasts
- Vivek: run thermal simulation and share rack heatmap (ETA EOD).
- Marissa: I'll loop in commercial to codify burst SLO/credits; please prepare a short note for procurement.
- Anya: Redwood will provide a daily CSV telemetry feed for burst windows (we'll expose a signed S3 URL per day).

I'll schedule a 30-min follow up on Monday to lock the final commitment and get procurement sign-off.

Hannah
Senior Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
